items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to present
notes: and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on the subject land known as 8196 Wellington Road 19 in the former Township of West Garafraxa.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from “A” Agricultural and “EP” Environmental Protection to “A” Agricultural Exception and “EP” Environmental Protection on the retained parcel to restrict residential uses.

Furthermore, the amendment will seek to permit a maximum floor area of 6.6% for accessory buildings on the severed parcel, and to recognize the height of the existing accessory building (barn) measuring 10.5 metres.

The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to facilitate a farm dwelling surplus severance and to recognize existing buildings on the severed parcel.
The zoning amendment is a condition of approval of the County of Wellington Land Division Committee Application B86-23

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT).

He indicated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the adoption of the proposed zoning by-law amendment, a written request must be sent to the Municipal Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, ON, N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before February 22, 2024. A copy of the notice was also advertised in the Wellington Advertiser on February 22, 2024. She confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on February 22, 2024.
Mayor Watters called on Jeff Buisman from Van Harten Surveying to introduce the application. J. Buisman provided an overview of the farm surplus dwelling proposal.
Mayor Watters indicated there are no registered delegations and asked if there was anyone present wishing to speak to the application.
There being no delegations, Mayor Watters offered Council an opportunity to ask any questions of the applicant or staff.
In response to a question from Councillor MacDonald, J. Buisman indicated the existing accessory farm structures are empty and primarily used for storage.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the by-law at a future Council meeting.
Mayor Watters declared the meeting closed and continued with the regular agenda.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters provided an update on recent activities from the County’s Planning Committee, including a new home energy efficiency program aimed at lowering green house gases emissions through energy retrofits, the development of a County listing of all residential development activity within the County, completion of the OPA 119 project, and the establishment of a Planning Innovation Lab, using the current staff compliment to provide a forum for a planning think tank.
Mayor Watters responded to a question related to the deferral of the pavilion project at the Museum.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Members of Council provided updates on recent initiatives and activities underway by Safe Communities, the Fergus BIA, Farm Safety, and the Lions Home and Leisure Show.

items.title: Staci Barron appeared before Council regarding the draft Noise By-law,
notes: questioning the wording, the lack of public engagement and input from the Economic Prosperity & Growth Committee, and the absence of decibel measurements and reading equipment.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. However, any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate discussion and/or action.

Councillor Adams indicated she has questions related to item 11.1, the January 29th Council minutes and the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee minutes and item 11.6, Emergency Sanitary Sewer Replacement on Metcalfe Street in Elora.

Councilllor Adams asked staff to confirm traffic concerns in the Strathallan area will be looked at in more detail in the future. In response, Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services indicated there are current initiatives underway related to St. Joseph School and there will be opportunities through the development process for further study of traffic safety and management.
Councillor Wilton noted the recorded vote was omitted from the January 29th minutes.

Councillor Adams asked for clarification regarding discussions at the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee referencing the previous strategic plan. Dan Wilson, CAO indicated the current business plan and strategic plan are being used to formulate the workplan, the reference to the previous strategic plan was for the purposes of outlining past accomplishments.

Councillor Adams asked for clarification on the source of the issues with respect to the Emergency Sanitary Sewer Replacement on Metcalfe Street in Elora. Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services indicated the repairs were completed in phases and the scope of the project expanded as more information became available. He indicated the concrete corrosion is not uncommon where there are high concentrations of hydrogen sulphate gas in the sewer environment.

items.title: Decision Report - South Fergus Secondary Plan (OPA 14) and Master
notes: Environmental Servicing Plan (MESP)
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development introduced Dave Aston and Emily Elliott from MHBC Planning Consultants on behalf of the land owners.

Dave Aston, Planner, MHBC Planning Consultants outlined the purpose of the Secondary Plan and the Master Environmental Servicing Plan (MESP) and provided an overview of the public consultation process and the feedback received, the draft Secondary Plan, including proposed land uses and amendments, the recommendations and implementation from the MESP and the next steps in the process.

D. Aston responded to questions regarding changes made from the comments/feedback received, the suggested locations of the community and neighbourhood parks, the use of design guidelines, designs encouraging active transportation, and design steps taken to interface the urban area with the agricultural area.

Members of Council expressed the importance of community connectivity, a safe highway 6 crossing, the importance of a welcoming and eye-pleasing gateway to the community, and the importance of park locations in close proximity to high density housing.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 7:37 pm.

B. Salmon provided an overview of the report, indicating the effect of the amendment is to implement detailed land use plans and policies to guide orderly development of the remaining designated greenfield land in South Fergus. He noted the South Fergus Secondary Plan provides a conceptual framework for the area and addresses the mix, arrangement and density of land uses, collector road network, size and location of parks and school sites, the location of major services, and the natural heritage network.

B. Salmon and D. Aston continued to respond to questions regarding the incorporation of the public comments received in the Secondary Plan, regulations regarding park land dedication, and timing of the community planning permitting system.
